Playbook.name: Windows — Ingress Tool Transfer via LOLBin - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Command and Control / Ingress Tool Transfer

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A living-off-the-land binary was used to download a file - certutil -urlcache, bitsadmin /transfer, curl/wget to a remote URL, or PowerShell DownloadFile. Triage question: is an attacker pulling a payload/tool onto the host, or a legitimate admin/update download?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: LOLBin downloads fetch attacker tooling while evading download controls - a common second-stage step.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: LOLBin download
Signal.Details: certutil/bitsadmin/curl/wget/PowerShell download of a remote file.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the LOLBin download fetched attacker tooling or a legitimate file.

Step.name: Confirm the download command and URL
Step.Purpose: The command reveals the tool and the remote URL/destination.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE (cl LIKE "*certutil*" AND (cl LIKE "*urlcache*" OR cl LIKE "*-f*http*")) OR (cl LIKE "*bitsadmin*" AND cl LIKE "*transfer*") OR ((cl LIKE "*curl*" OR cl LIKE "*wget*") AND cl LIKE "*http*") OR (cl LIKE "*downloadfile*" OR cl LIKE "*downloadstring*" OR cl LIKE "*invoke-webrequest*") | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, user.name, process.command_line | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: The URL matters: a raw IP, a paste site, or an unusual domain fetching an .exe/.dll/.ps1 to temp/appdata = malicious. An internal update server or a signed vendor URL is likely benign. Note the destination path.

Step.name: Did the downloaded file then execute
Step.Purpose: A download immediately followed by execution of the fetched file is the tool-transfer-then-run chain.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | WHERE process.parent.name RLIKE "(?i)(cmd|powershell|pwsh|certutil|bitsadmin).*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A new process from temp/appdata spawned shortly after the download confirms the transferred tool ran - escalate to IR.

Node.Condition: Download of an executable/script from a suspicious URL (raw IP/paste site/unusual domain) to temp/appdata, especially if it then executed.
A download from an internal update server or signed vendor URL by an admin/updater.
LOLBin download with an unclear URL/destination.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-INGRESS-CMD, INV-02-INGRESS-EXEC to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the source; close as false_positive.
Isolate the host; capture the downloaded file; open IR.
Block the URL/IP; hunt the same download elsewhere.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured job downloading via LOLBin unnecessarily.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
